7310.t: From κάμηλος (kắmēlos, “camel”) + πάρδαλις (pắrdălĭs, “leopard”); from the fact that a giraffe has a long neck like a camel and is spotted like a leopard.

7334.t: From καταγελάω (kătăgelắō, “to mock; to jeer”), from κατα- (kătă-, “against”) + γελάω (gelắō, “to laugh at”).

7312.t: Possibly an Old Iranian borrowing, from Proto-Iranian *kamarā- (“something curved”), from *kamárati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kmárati, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kh₂em- (“to bend, curve”).

7351.t: From καταλύω (katalúō, “loosen, destroy; stay the night”) + -της (-tēs, noun-forming suffix)

7313.t: κάρπασος (kárpăsos) [from the Hebrew כַּרְפַּס (karpás, “a type of expensive fabric made of cotton”)] + -ινος (-inos)

7317.t: From κάρος (kắros, “heavy sleep, torpor”) + -όω (-óō, verbal suffix).

7326.t: From the root of καθίστημι (kathístēmi) + -σις (-sis); also analyzable as κατα- (kata-) + στάσις (stásis).
